questions.question: Q1 What structural defect can occur if the wire bonding tool presses down onto a pad with way too much ultrasonic force?

explanations.a: Frequency settings handle timing bounds; they do not alter metal trace dimensions.
explanations.b: Correct! Excessive force or vibration can crack the fragile crystalline silicon layer directly underneath the pad.
explanations.c: Plasma boundaries relate to deposition chambers, not circuit probing beds.
explanations.d: Design files remain locked inside non-volatile software server domains.

questions.question: Q2 What can happen if the protective plastic compound and the internal silicon die expand at wildly different rates when heated?

answers.a: The wire tracks will automatically turn into silicon glass
answers.b: The wire joints can snap or pull off due to high internal stress
answers.c: The chip will automatically wipe its hardcoded memory
answers.d: The dicing saw tape will melt inside the molding machine

explanations.a: Dicing tool dynamics dictate how fast saws slice through base materials.
explanations.b: Correct! Disproportionate expansion rates (a CTE mismatch) create heavy pulling forces that snap the wire bonds.
explanations.c: RPM indicators track centrifugal parameters on spin cleaning units.
explanations.d: Raster step timings match parameter profiles inside scanner assemblies.

questions.question: Q3 What is the 'Popcorn Effect' in microchip package failures?

answers.a: The pleasant clicking noise a dicing saw makes during clean cuts
answers.b: Trapped moisture expanding into steam during high-heat soldering, cracking the package body open
answers.c: When gold bonding wires accidentally melt back into raw copper atoms
answers.d: When a chip automatically shifts into a premium speed grade

explanations.a: Acid reactions depend on liquid mixture distributions in chemical hoods.
explanations.b: Correct! Trapped internal moisture vaporizes and expands explosively during board assembly thermal reflow.
explanations.c: Clock limits remain fixed by test engineering console choices.
explanations.d: The physical die count is permanently fixed by the initial lithography step layout.

questions.question: Q4 What is a 'wire sweep' defect during the encapsulation molding phase?

answers.a: When a diamond saw blade cuts through a gold connection line
answers.b: When the fast-flowing liquid plastic resin bends closely spaced wire loops into each other, causing short circuits
answers.c: When an operator manually polishes the surface of the wafer chuck
answers.d: When the tester pins are turned off to get a perfect yield percentage

explanations.a: Correct! High-velocity liquid resin flow can mechanically shift or bend long, closely spaced wire loops into contact.
explanations.b: Testing rules remain mandatory for every production wafer lot.
explanations.c: Mapping creates diagnostic records; it does not trigger automatic physical repairs.
explanations.d: Freight weights depend on material densities and packaging materials choices.

questions.question: Q5 Why is copper wire bonding cheaper but physically harder to configure than traditional gold wire bonding?

answers.a: Copper wire can only work inside freezing environments
answers.b: Copper is physically stiffer and harder than gold, requiring careful pressure adjustments to avoid pad damage
answers.c: Copper melts at a much lower temperature than packaging plastic
answers.d: Copper requires special liquid acids to be sprayed onto the wafer continuously

explanations.a: The die functions safely at baseline rules and should not be thrown away.
explanations.b: Correct! The material hardness of copper requires tight calibration of bonding forces to prevent silicon cracking.
explanations.c: Finished wafers cannot go backward into early metal deposition tools.
explanations.d: Placing slow chips into demanding high-speed slots causes immediate server crashes.

questions.question: Q6 What primary event happens inside the machine tool during the 'transfer molding' phase?

answers.a: A diamond blade rotates at 30,000 RPM to isolate individual dies
answers.b: Hot liquid plastic resin is injected under heavy pressure to seal the chip assembly
answers.c: Microscopic gold wires are stitched using high-frequency sound energy
answers.d: Electronic needles touch landing pads to check internal timing parameters

explanations.a: This defines static geometric resistance boundaries for wiring lines.
explanations.b: Correct! Liquefied epoxy resin flows into a hot mold cavity under pressure to enclose the die assembly.
explanations.c: This calculates macroscopic acceleration metrics in mechanical domains.
explanations.d: This relates voltage to current and resistance across simple passive networks.

questions.question: Q7 How does a thermosonic wire bonder create the very first connection point when using gold wire?

answers.a: By using an electrical spark to melt the wire tip into a ball, then mashing it down with force and vibration
answers.b: By freezing the wire until it adheres to the pad via cryogenic suction
answers.c: By spraying a layer of toxic acid onto the pad to melt the silicon layer
answers.d: By rotating the substrate chuck at 5000 RPM until friction melts the frame

explanations.a: Cosmetic micro-scratches are handled by packaging or sorting visual tool inspects.
explanations.b: Correct! An electrical flame-off melts the wire end into a ball, which is then welded using ultrasonic sound energy.
explanations.c: Fast components are rewarded with high speed bin status grades.
explanations.d: A dead wafer represents a catastrophic process lot yield failure condition.

questions.question: Q8 Why is gold wire historically selected for critical wire bonding applications despite its high cost?

answers.a: It dissolves instantly inside epoxy molding compound mixtures
answers.b: It combines excellent electrical conductivity with superb resistance to oxidation
answers.c: It is the hardest metal known, preventing die cratering entirely
answers.d: It transforms into a semiconductor when heated above one hundred degrees

explanations.a: Plasma loops are restricted to enclosed PVD deposition tool cavities.
explanations.b: Correct! Gold handles micro-scale connections smoothly and never oxidizes or corrodes over time.
explanations.c: Residue clearing requires physical acid etching runs, not thermal tests.
explanations.d: Wafer diameter is fixed by raw mechanical ingot slicing rules.

questions.question: Q9 What does a very low 'Bond Pull Strength' reading indicate during structural inspection testing?

answers.a: The package has achieved a perfect, air-tight environmental seal
answers.b: The wire connection joint is weak and likely to break or lift off under stress
answers.c: The test frequency parameters need to be cranked up immediately
answers.d: The silicon die has grown too large for its outer plastic housing layout

explanations.a: Yield scores cannot exceed 100% of the total available die count.
explanations.b: Correct! Low pull force values highlight weak metal welds that are prone to structural failures.
explanations.c: 20% represents the scrap factor or failure drop metrics, not the yield.
explanations.d: This value does not match the proportion of functional components.

questions.question: Q10 What tuning strategy achieves the best balance of reliable wire joints and high manufacturing yields?

answers.a: Cranking the ultrasonic force to absolute maximum right from the start
answers.b: Adjusting force and molding temperatures to find the safest windows before cracks or shorts occur
answers.c: Disabling all checking monitors to log an artificial perfect score
answers.d: Shaking the assembly tool rapidly to throw loose atoms into alignment

explanations.a: Blasting maximum rules right away destroys functional margins, causing yield numbers to crater.
explanations.b: Correct! Proper calibration balances bond strength against stress limits to prevent chip failures.
explanations.c: Disabling sensor tracks creates false data logs, causing bad chips to break in user hands.
explanations.d: Mechanical shaking breaks probe needle arrays and fractures delicate silicon surfaces.
